what_happened: The job was meant to stop stalled agents early, so a stuck agent would not use the whole deadline. It was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier gave two major findings. First, the stall window is shorter than the agent's configured Bash tool time limit (procs.rs stall_window; claude.rs:364-382), so a slow but healthy agent running a long command would be killed as stalled. Second, the reading did not match the request, so the passing criteria do not show the request was met. No acceptance criteria are listed as unmet and no checks are listed as failed. The stored fields don't say which part of the request the reading got wrong.
cause: Nothing in code relates a new time threshold to the existing time limits it must respect. The stall window and the Bash tool limit are set in separate places (procs.rs and claude.rs), and no check requires one to be longer than the other. The accepted reading was not compared with the request's wording, so criteria were written that pass without covering the intent. A "stalled" signal that does not account for legitimately silent long commands is a design gap, and only the verifier's read at the final verdict found it. This is an inference, since the stored fields don't show the request text or the reading.
prevention: Add a code check, such as a unit test or a startup validation, that derives the stall window from the configured Bash tool time limit and fails if the window is not strictly longer, or if an agent with an active tool call is counted as stalled. Also require that a reading for any timeout or early-stop request lists every existing time limit it interacts with and has a behavior criterion for the case of a slow but healthy agent running a long tool call. The stall detector should count tool activity as progress.
proposed_request: Stop stalled agents early instead of using the full deadline, without ever killing a healthy agent. Outcome: an agent that makes no progress is stopped and the job records a clear "stalled" reason. An agent that is running a long but legitimate tool call, up to the configured Bash tool time limit, is never treated as stalled. The stall window must be longer than the Bash tool time limit, or must count an active tool call as progress. This must be enforced in code, with one place that holds both values and a test that fails if the window is not longer than the tool limit. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fake agent that stays silent past the stall window gets stopped early and the job records the stalled reason; (2) a test with a fake agent running a tool call that lasts longer than the stall window, but within the tool limit, is not stopped; (3) the stall window is tied to the Bash tool time limit in config or code, not a separate constant; (4) the change description lists the existing time limits checked and the commands actually run.
